title: Tool-Making and Self-Evolving LLM Agents in Low-Latency Systems
reason: 核心贡献是让软件代理利用真实执行轨迹和带标签的测试反馈，生成、修复并维护可复用的版本化工具，以替代逐请求写代码。跨模型组件消融、留出集测试和生产对照支持其效果；残余错误分析明确了规范质量的限制，但跨业务泛化尚未验证。另有基于筛选轨迹的辅助微调，并验证了无工具时的回退能力。工具上线仍需人工审核，未展示改进机制自身的演化。
abstract: Production LLM agents often waste latency and reliability by regenerating code for the same procedural steps on every request. We replace this inference-time coding loop with an agentic tool-making pipeline that compiles repeated SOP steps into validated, versioned tools before deployment. The tool-maker grounds synthesis in the live environment as it collects execution traces, observes backend schemas and values, generates candidate tools, and repairs them against labeled cases. At runtime, the production agent calls these tools directly and falls back to code generation only when needed. We deploy the approach in a Fulfillment Center alarm-triage system, where an agent diagnoses alarms against a 44-node SOP over heterogeneous metric backends. In production, tool calls reduce p50 latency by 42%. On 1500 historical alarms, they reduce end-to-end error rate by up to 53% by suppressing run-to-run variance in repeated steps. Because tools return compact structured verdicts, they also enable a simpler direct-call architecture, reducing p50 latency by a further 62% in a controlled ablation. Versioned tools also improve auditability and expose specification gaps and upstream data drift. Our results show that agents that build and maintain their own tool libraries, a key element of self-evolving agents, can make industrial LLM systems faster, more reliable, and easier to operate.
evidence: We replace this inference-time coding loop with an agentic tool-making pipeline that compiles repeated SOP steps into validated, versioned tools before deployment.
result: In production, tool calls reduce p50 latency by 42%.
